reports.title: Palo Alto Networks Reports Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: Palo Alto Networks provides guidance based on current market conditions and expectations.

desk.headline: Revenue up 39% to $3.44bn, beat; full-year revenue and EPS outlook raised; $4.5bn Applied Compute deal

other.label: GAAP diluted EPS
other.change: vs $0.47; includes a one-time tax benefit

results: Revenue grew 39% to $3.44bn (about $3.31bn expected); subscription and support sales rose 40% to $2.85bn and product sales 37% to $595m.
Next-Generation Security ARR, the company's key growth gauge, rose 66% to $9.73bn; contracted future revenue (RPO) rose 35% to $21.0bn.

Adjusted EPS rose to $1.05 from $0.93, ahead of the $0.97 expected; GAAP EPS of $0.57 was lifted by a $457m tax benefit, while GAAP operating income fell to $96m on higher amortisation and share-based pay after the CyberArk deal.
Operating cash flow was $1.93bn and adjusted free cash flow $1.94bn, a 56.2% margin.
Agreed to buy Applied Compute, an open-weight AI model platform, in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5bn, expected to close in fiscal Q3.

guidance.summary: Full-year fiscal 2027 revenue, ARR and adjusted EPS ranges were all raised from the September outlook; operating margin (29.5%) and free cash flow margin (38%) targets were kept. A first Q2 outlook calls for revenue of $3.53-3.55bn, up 36-37%.

points: CEO Nikesh Arora described an unusually dangerous threat environment, with AI helping attackers find serious software flaws at close to seven times last year's monthly rate.
A record of about 170 large customers moved onto the full platform in the quarter; these customers make up about two-thirds of Next-Generation Security ARR.
Applied Compute already has over $100m of annualised revenue and is expected to add more than $1bn to ARR by fiscal 2029, but will cut operating margin by up to 1 point in FY27 and 2 points in FY28.
Gross margin slipped 1.7 points to 75.2% on costlier hardware components and a shift to cloud-delivered products, a pressure expected to last through the year.
The acquired CyberArk identity business grew 23% on a like-for-like basis and is expected to reach group-level margins in about 12 months, sooner than first planned.
call.source: Call coverage: BigGo Finance call summary (18 Nov 2026), SiliconANGLE and Seeking Alpha (18 Nov 2026); no prepared remarks filed

watch: Closing of the Applied Compute deal and how much it weighs on margins and data-centre spending.
Whether gross margin keeps falling as hardware component costs rise.
Delivery against the raised $11.5bn year-end ARR target.
